Industry observers note that canadian gamblers have spent the past two years quietly rerouting their deposits from Interac transfers and prepaid vouchers to Bitcoin wallets. The shift is practical, driven primarily by settlement speed. A bank e-transfer can sit in processing over a long weekend, while a BTC confirmation clears in roughly ten minutes regardless of province or statutory holiday. Searches for btc casinos and btc casino online have climbed accordingly, though the operators behind those results vary wildly in licensing, game fairness, and how seriously they treat withdrawal limits.

Roobet has built its reputation as the category’s reference point. Its BTC casino model skips fiat rails entirely, crediting deposits as soon as a transaction confirms on-chain rather than waiting for a payment processor to batch it overnight. That design choice is a big reason it keeps surfacing at the top of Canadian comparison lists, even against operators with longer track records.

Deposits move at network speed, which also means there is no chargeback mechanism once a transaction confirms. Players carry the volatility themselves between deposit and cashout, and a platform that converts to stablecoins at deposit removes that exposure in a way a straight BTC balance does not. The sector’s shift toward stablecoin settlement largely reflects players being burned by holding BTC through a losing session during a price drop. Withdrawal limits tell a similar story: a casino that caps daily cashouts low enough to slow a winning streak is usually managing its own liquidity risk. So users should be looking at the fine print on payout ceilings, which deserve more attention than the headline bonus.

Ranked side by side, the gap is less about game count and more about withdrawal friction and Canadian access.

Provably fair systems let a player verify, after the fact, that a game’s outcome wasn’t altered after they placed their bet, using a published seed and hash. It is a meaningful trust layer, but it only confirms a round wasn’t tampered with, not that the house edge is favorable. Canadian players comparing operators against real-money alternatives still need to check return-to-player rates game by game, since a verifiable algorithm and a generous payout rate are separate questions that marketing copy tends to blur.

Sources indicate that most offshore crypto casinos serving Canadians are licensed through the Kahnawake Gaming Commission, based in Mohawk Territory in Quebec, which has issued gambling licenses since 1999. Ontario is the exception: since April 2022 it has run its own regulated online market through iGaming Ontario, meaning operators without an Ontario registration are technically off-limits to residents there, even if the rest of the country can reach them freely. That patchwork is why “player protection” means something different depending on which province a deposit originates in.

None of that structure fixes the harder problem: crypto deposits remove the natural friction that used to slow a losing streak. A platform worth using still publishes deposit limits and self-exclusion tools on the same page as its game lobby, not buried three clicks deep. That detail tells a player more about the platform’s integrity than any welcome offer does.

Bitcoin’s mining difficulty falls 9%, easing pressure on miners

The November 14 adjustment reversed most of October’s difficulty increases. Expected coin earnings improve, but profits still depend on price, fees and costs.

Industry observers note that bitcoin’s mining difficulty fell 9.1% on November 14, reversing most of the extra computational burden added by October’s two increases. The completed reset increases the chance that a given amount of computing work earns a block reward, providing immediate computational relief for operating miners.

According to recent reports, the adjustment took effect at block 975,744, timestamped 05:02:50 UTC. Difficulty dropped from 148.36 trillion to 134.82 trillion, according to Mempool’s adjustment history.

Bitcoin recalculates difficulty every 2,016 blocks to target an average interval of roughly ten minutes.

Sources indicate that october’s increases had lifted difficulty by a combined 11.8% from its October 3 level of 132.72 trillion. The first increase, on October 16, was about 5.9%; the second, on October 29, added about 5.5%.

In a recent development, the November cut removed 86.5% of the increase accumulated across those two adjustments. Difficulty now sits just 1.6% above the October 3 baseline. The reset therefore unwinds most of that added burden without taking difficulty all the way back to its earlier level.

The completed November 14 reset leaves difficulty 1.59% above October 3. Levels are in trillions (T), rounded to three decimals in labels. Four discrete 2026 retargets; bars begin at zero.

Source: Mempool difficulty-adjustment history.

At unchanged block subsidy and average transaction fees per block, the old-to-new difficulty ratio implies 10% higher expected BTC earnings per unit of computing power.

According to recent reports, the gain is larger than the 9.13% difficulty decline because earnings per hash move inversely with difficulty. Dividing the previous difficulty by the new level gives about 1.1004, meaning the same work has a higher expected reward under those fixed assumptions. It is a calculation of gross expected earnings, rather than a measured increase in a miner’s receipts or profit.

In the last two market cycles, Bitcoin [BTC] formed a bottom after roughly six consecutive weekly red candles, followed by strong rebound rallies. This time, the pattern is starting to look similar. Bitcoin has now had six red weekly candles, with its price dropping from $85k to $65k. The RSI is also showing oversold levels, adding to the case for a potential rebound.

However, with bearish on-chain signals and increased macro uncertainty, BTC may struggle to repeat its previous recovery, putting that $60k support at greater risk.

Could a break below $60k trigger a deeper correction?

As discussed earlier, strong buying support is still missing. Weak ETF flows, a negative Coinbase Premium Index, and extreme fear are all indicative of weakening demand. On top of that, STH whales also have almost $8 billion in unrealized losses to sell ahead of Anthropic’s IPO. The key takeaway? The risk does go beyond a price breakdown. If Bitcoin breaks below $60k, that could cause more than $2.6 billion in long liquidation. This can cause a chain reaction of liquidation, which will cause more downwards pressure. While such a flush may bring BTC closer to a cycle bottom, a quick rebound is far from guaranteed.

Ultimately, BTC’s ability to hold $60k will be a key test, especially with Anthropic’s IPO adding to the FUD.

Cardano DReps have rejected a proposal by Toto Finance to spend 22 million ADA from the Cardano treasury on a "Strategic Copper Reserve.".

The vote closed on Nov. 15, and DReps holding 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, according to Cardano governance data. DReps with 20.02 million ADA voted in favor of it.

DRep John MacPherson was among those who voted "No," and he explained his decision in a post on X.

MacPherson wrote that he is not against real-world assets on Cardano. Still, he said the proposal asks the treasury "to take on both the copper price and the ada price," and Toto Finance would collect "up to about 3.4M ada in fees.".

At the same time, MacPherson said that the proposal is “more honest about its risks than most.”.

Toto Finance, a company led by Monty Metzger, submitted the proposal on Oct. 15. ADA is trading at $0.152 on Monday, and the requested 22 million ADA is now worth around $3.3 million.

The plan was to buy copper with 14.72 million ADA and store it in a warehouse near Fresh Orleans. Toto Finance wanted to issue one CuTT token for each pound of copper. The metal would be sold in 18 to 24 months.

The Cardano Foundation, which votes as a DRep, revealed its "No" vote in October.

"We recognize the opportunity in real-world asset tokenization; however, this proposal places 22,000,000 ada under the recipient's sole control to fund a fee-heavy concentrated commodity position whose safeguards are not yet in place," the foundation wrote.

Three members of the Constitutional Committee voted "No," and the other four members did not vote.

Crypto commentator Ingeniero Cripto agreed with MacPherson in the replies under his post. He called the "double exposure" to the prices of copper and ADA the key problem of the proposal, as the Cardano treasury already holds ADA.

According to him, RWAs on Cardano make sense, but “funding the asset itself is a different question than funding the rails.”.

It has been revealed that thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking feedback on restrictions that could significantly change how customers move stablecoins through regulated digital-asset operators. The proposed rules would generally limit eligible transfers into and out of a customer's account to 5 million baht per day in each direction, while requiring wallets at both ends to belong to that customer.

Recent findings suggest that this is a consultation, not a rule that has already taken effect. The details, exemptions and eventual text matter more than the headline dollar equivalent, especially for businesses using stablecoins for legitimate cross-border payments.

In its November 12 announcement, the Thai SEC stated the draft aims to reduce the risk that regulated crypto businesses facilitate money laundering, cybercrime or circumvention of cross-border transfer rules. The proposal would generally require stablecoins entering or leaving a customer's account at a digital-asset operator to come from, or go to, an account or wallet verified as belonging to that same person.

The draft also calls for controls aligned with the Travel Rule, screening for risky wallets and transaction monitoring. Those measures aim to improve traceability where a licensed intermediary is involved. They do not mean all movements of stablecoins across every blockchain would suddenly be visible to, or controlled by, one Thai exchange.

Under the proposal, inbound and outbound transfers would each be limited separately to 5 million baht per customer, per day, with each operator. The SEC's announcement also describes exemptions, including qualifying transfers between the customer's own accounts at regulated operators, certain regulated businesses and approved liquidity-provision activities. The exact scope depends on the final regulation and whether participants satisfy the relevant requirements.

According to recent reports, that nuance is easy to lose in a short headline. It would be inaccurate to say Thailand is proposing a universal daily blockchain transfer limit, or that every business must stop moving more than that amount under all circumstances. The consultation is specifically focused on activity conducted through supervised digital-asset operators.

According to recent reports, stablecoins have become useful tools for businesses moving money across borders, particularly where traditional transfers are expensive or slow. NewsBTC's report on Bitso Business's stablecoin payments shows the commercial use case behind this growth. For such companies, wallet verification and transfer limits create compliance work that must fit alongside existing customer checks.

In a recent development, the risk is that rules designed to catch illicit activity could also make ordinary, lawful operations cumbersome if identity matching is difficult or exceptions are unclear. The regulator, meanwhile, has a legitimate interest in ensuring supervised firms know who is using their systems. That tension is precisely what a public consultation is supposed to examine.

The SEC has invited feedback through November 26, 2026. Businesses should review the official draft rather than rely on simplified social-media summaries, particularly when deciding whether their specific transaction flows would be covered. The same distinction between technology and regulated access appears in NewsBTC's coverage of USDC on Solana through Samsung Wallet.

Sources indicate that thailand's proposal reflects a growing regulatory emphasis on the point where blockchain assets interact with licensed businesses. Whether the final rules strike the intended balance will depend on clear exemptions, workable verification and evidence that the controls reduce risk without unnecessarily obstructing legitimate payments.

Home » Esports » Project Helix Xbox Console Will Run PC Games: What It Means for Web3.

Microsoft VP Jason Ronald details how the next-gen console merges Xbox libraries with PC gaming.

Industry observers note that microsoft has officially clarified its vision for the upcoming Project Helix Xbox console, confirming in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine that the next-generation system is built to run both traditional Xbox libraries and PC games. A hybrid shift could also open new doors for Web3 gaming.

It has been revealed that as Microsoft celebrates Xbox’s 25th anniversary, the manufacturer has shared fresh architectural details about the Project Helix Xbox console, its upcoming next-generation console. When Microsoft first introduced the project earlier this year, it confirmed that the new system would bring Xbox and PC gaming closer together. This led many to assume that Helix would essentially be a Windows gaming PC packaged in a console design.

In a four-page Q&A inside the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, Vice President of Next Generation Jason Ronald pushed back directly against that framing.

“Project Helix is designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC,” Ronald stated. “It is not a PC that can also play console games.”.

For Microsoft, the distinction comes down to removing the friction traditionally associated with PC gaming, such as driver management, multiple launchers, and complex configuration menus, while keeping deeper controls accessible for enthusiasts.

According to recent reports, “The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games,” Ronald explained. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.”.

According to Ronald and the anniversary feature, Project Helix is being built around several core pillars:.

Project Helix, which Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has previously described as a broader “family of devices” rather than a single box, is taking shape during a turbulent stretch for Microsoft’s gaming division.

After taking the helm earlier in 2026, Sharma oversaw major restructuring, studio closures, and layoffs, candidly remarking in July that the Xbox brand was “not healthy.” Simultaneously, ongoing global memory and storage component shortages have pushed up manufacturing costs across the hardware industry, prompting some players to urge both Microsoft and Sony to delay next-gen launches until prices stabilize.

Ronald acknowledged those supply-chain headwinds, calling the current hardware environment “brutal,” though he argued that the constraints are forcing Xbox engineers to innovate rather than simply throw costlier components at the machine.

The technology maps rainfall worldwide at 15-minute intervals, offering new tools for studying disasters in poorly monitored regions.

Google DeepMind has opened access to an artificial intelligence system that tracks rainfall worldwide, potentially helping researchers monitor floods and droughts in regions with limited weather infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that the organization revealed on Nov. 13 that researchers and developers can now access historical records and continuously updated data from PARDIG, its AI-powered global precipitation monitoring system.

The technology combines satellite observations and atmospheric data to estimate rainfall every 15 minutes across a global grid with roughly 10-kilometer resolution.

Its release could expand access to rainfall intelligence in developing countries and remote regions where limited weather radar coverage makes it difficult to track storms, flooding and prolonged dry spells.

Google stated PARDIG learns from precipitation measurements collected by NASA's Global Precipitation Measurement satellite and uses additional satellite imagery and atmospheric information to estimate rainfall across the planet.

Unlike conventional monitoring systems that depend heavily on ground-based weather stations, PARDIG can generate estimates over oceans and regions with sparse observation networks.

The dataset also supports Google's WeatherNext 3 forecasting model, which uses PARDIG-generated rainfall information during training.

Researchers can access historical rainfall records dating back to 1999, alongside a separate dataset covering 2016 to the present.

Google has released both under a Creative Commons license that permits commercial reuse with attribution, potentially allowing companies to incorporate the information into agricultural monitoring, water management and disaster-risk applications.

DeepMind mentioned PARDIG achieved more than 30% higher hourly precipitation detection skill than NASA's IMERG-Final dataset when measuring light-to-moderate rainfall.

The organization evaluated the system against radar networks in the United States, Europe and Japan, alongside observations from more than 36,000 weather stations worldwide.

Its research paper also reported improved identification of intense rainfall events, which existing global precipitation datasets can struggle to capture accurately.

These capabilities could help researchers develop more detailed models of extreme weather events, including flash floods, landslides and drought conditions.

Google highlighted the July 2025 Texas Hill Country floods as one example, comparing PARDIG's estimates with ground-based radar measurements and NASA's existing rainfall dataset.

However, the technology has limitations that could constrain its use during rapidly developing emergencies.

Although PARDIG estimates rainfall at 15-minute intervals, Google publishes its near-real-time data in six-hour batches, creating an average delay of about five hours between observation and availability.

XRP Ledger Foundation Director of Community Hussein Zangana (Vet) shared a tidbit of XRPL's early history in a recent X post.

Vet noted that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) still carries traces of Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design, highlighting two features.

According to recent reports, in 2011, three engineers—David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb, and Arthur Britto—began developing the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Fascinated by Bitcoin, they set out to create a better version that improved upon its limitations—with the goal of creating a digital asset that was more sustainable and built specifically for payments.

As reported, the first line of code for the core of what would become the XRP Ledger (XRPL) was written by David Schwartz, who is Ripple CTO emeritus, about 15 years ago, on November 11, 2011.

Vet delves into the earliest part of XRP Ledger history, noting that 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, wrote. Vet added that Jed McCaleb also copied Satoshi’s timekeeping code into the XRPL, even including one of the Bitcoin creator’s comments shared as a screenshot.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily? 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote. Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including one of Satoshi's comments. By the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone. In December 2014, Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment. Two design choices of Satoshi still remain on the XRPL and all of us use at least one of it. Signature curve secp256k1 (we also support Ed25519 thus not everyone uses this) and how XRPL addresses are generated from the public key with SHA-256 followed by RIPEMD-160, that's what all of us use.

The quote "Never go to sea with two chronometers; take one or three" is a classic maritime adage famously included by Satoshi Nakamoto (the pseudonymous creator of Bitcoin) within the Bitcoin source code.

According to recent reports, vet explained that by the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone from the XRP Ledger. In December 2014, former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment.

Sources indicate that however, two of Satoshi's design choices still remain on the XRP Ledger: the first is the secp256k1 signature curve, which Bitcoin uses and which the XRP Ledger continues to support. However, the ledger also supports Ed25519, meaning not every XRPL user relies on secp256k1.

"I remember David saying they used secp256k1 so no one would doubt the security because it's the same as Bitcoin's, etc.," Vet stated, citing the insight of the Ripple CTO emeritus on secp256k1, adding, "Lots of interesting things to dig into from the early days.".

The second is the method used to generate XRP Ledger addresses from public keys. The process applies SHA-256 hashing followed by RIPEMD-160, a design inherited from Bitcoin that remains common to all XRPL addresses.

Asked why the timekeeping code and Satoshi's comment were removed, Vet explained that this became leftover code as new code was introduced, so it was cleaned up.

It has been revealed that twenty One Capital has reported net income of about $1.09 billion for the third quarter, a figure that might look extraordinary for a Bitcoin-focused company. But nearly all of that profit came from changes in the fair value of its Bitcoin holdings rather than cash generated by selling services. That makes the result a useful lesson in how digital-asset treasury accounting can obscure the difference between holding an appreciated asset and operating a profitable business.

Neither figure should be ignored. Bitcoin holdings can create real economic value, but marked-to-market gains can reverse quickly when prices change.

According to The Block's account of Twenty One Capital's filing, the company reported $1.087 billion in quarterly net income, driven largely by around $1.093 billion in fair-value increases on Bitcoin. At the same time, it recorded an operating loss of approximately $4.8 million and interest expense near $1.34 million.

In a recent development, that contrast is the heart of the story. An asset can become more valuable on the balance sheet without generating money to pay salaries or service borrowing costs. Accounting rules may require those changes to appear in reported earnings, but investors still need to separate recurring business performance from market revaluation when assessing sustainability.

Twenty One Capital reported holding 43,514 BTC at September 30, with its holdings valued using a Bitcoin price around $83,700 at the reporting date. The company also disclosed approximately $102.8 million in cash and $486.5 million of convertible-note principal collateralised by a portion of its Bitcoin. Those liabilities and collateral arrangements are important because holding a volatile asset alongside debt creates distinct liquidity and financing considerations.

Recent findings suggest that A higher Bitcoin price can make the balance sheet appear stronger. A lower price can compress asset values while obligations remain, potentially forcing management to reconsider capital allocation. That is why the composition of the treasury, maturity profile and collateral terms can be just as relevant as the headline quantity of BTC.

Industry observers note that chief executive Rapha Zagury has made clear that asset appreciation and profits earned through operations are different. The manufacturer has discussed possible opportunities in mining, lending, treasury-related services and share repurchases. Those ideas could broaden its sources of income, but they should be treated as areas under consideration until the business publishes concrete agreements, operating milestones and results.

Industry observers note that other Bitcoin treasury companies face similar questions. NewsBTC's coverage of benchmark treatment for Strategy and Metaplanet highlights how public-market investors consider corporate exposure to Bitcoin through lenses that extend beyond the coin's price.

Industry observers note that the same filing showed a net loss for the first nine months of 2026, underscoring how results can swing with changing Bitcoin prices. Investors evaluating a treasury business should consider asset value per share, the effect of any new share or debt issuance, cash needs and whether proposed business lines eventually contribute positive operating cash flow.

It has been revealed that there is a market-wide backdrop too. Recent Bitcoin ETF redemptions covered by NewsBTC show that demand for BTC exposure can weaken abruptly. Twenty One Capital's quarterly statement is not evidence that the Bitcoin treasury model has either won or failed. It is evidence that accounting earnings can be dominated by the underlying asset — and that understanding the difference is essential.

Harvard University and Dartmouth College reported unchanged share counts in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter as a Bitcoin rally lifted the value of both stakes.

Harvard held 3.04 million shares of the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT), worth about $144.1 million at the end of September, while Dartmouth reported 201,531 shares valued at $9.5 million, according to Form 13F filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Harvard has reported the same IBIT share count since the end of March, after cutting its holdings by 43% in Q1 and 21% in Q4 2025. Dartmouth has reported the same 201,531 shares since first disclosing its Bitcoin ETF position in Q4 2025.

Harvard increased its share count in the State Street’s SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) nearly 20-fold in Q3, to 1.16 million from 58,862. The position was worth $442.2 million at the end of September.

Industry observers note that dartmouth again reported 304,803 shares of the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF and 178,148 shares of the Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF. The positions were worth $4.9 million and $4.5 million, respectively, at quarter-end.

According to recent reports, the steady university holdings contrasted with moves by major financial companies. Jane Street reduced its IBIT shares by 19% in Q3, while JPMorgan Chase increased the number of shares it held by 9.6%, according to their latest quarterly filings.

Recent findings suggest that kraken parent Payward has reported a sequential improvement in quarterly profitability even as its business remains smaller on several measures than it was a year earlier. The organization posted $60 million in adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026, up from $23 million in the previous quarter, alongside an expansion of its platform beyond conventional cryptocurrency trading.

Sources indicate that those results point to a business trying to diversify while navigating a difficult trading environment. They also require attention to the company's chosen metrics: adjusted EBITDA and its newly emphasised Total Platform Margin are not the same thing as statutory net profit or ordinary gross revenue.

In its November 13 financial update, Payward reported Total Platform Margin, or TPM, of $487 million, compared with $436 million in the second quarter. That represented 12% sequential growth, although TPM was also down 12% from a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $60 million from $23 million in Q2, while remaining substantially below the year-earlier result.

Recent findings suggest that payward has changed how it presents the business, replacing a previously highlighted adjusted-revenue measure with TPM. The company claims this approach deducts costs passed on to customers, including certain staking rewards, to provide a better view of what the platform retains. Investors should compare periods on consistent definitions rather than treating a renamed headline metric as automatically equivalent to prior revenue figures.

Total platform transaction volume reached about $353 billion, up 22% quarter on quarter, though down 30% from Q3 2025. Funded accounts increased to around 7.1 million, reflecting an expanding account base even as overall trading conditions remained challenging. The combination suggests growth in the number of customers does not necessarily translate into a proportional increase in transaction activity every quarter.

Sources indicate that the organization also highlighted transaction-based, asset-based and access-based sources of platform margin. Together, asset and access activity represented slightly more than half of TPM, indicating an effort to rely less exclusively on trading fees. Whether those businesses remain resilient through another difficult market cycle will be more telling than one period of sequential recovery.

It has been revealed that payward's broader ambitions include banking, asset management, services for other businesses and AI-driven financial tools. Its statement describes plans to introduce an agent-oriented layer intended to let customers authorise software to perform actions within programmed risk limits. Such a system raises practical questions about consent, error handling and how a customer reverses an unwanted automated action.

According to recent reports, newsBTC previously covered Payward's proposed move into European banking through Saldo, which illustrates how the company is seeking a wider relationship with customers than a trading account alone. These plans should not be confused with proof that every revealed product is already commercially available or licensed in every market.

Expanding into adjacent activities can smooth the effects of volatile crypto trading, but it can also introduce fresh costs and regulatory obligations. Payward's investment in Aave covered by NewsBTC is another example of the tech giant's interest in market infrastructure beyond centralised exchange transactions.

The next quarterly update should show whether TPM growth continues without depending on a short-lived jump in volumes, and how much of the improvement reaches the bottom line. For now, the Q3 release offers a mixed but informative picture: recovery from Q2, weaker comparisons with last year and a company making a deliberate bet on diversification.

Luxor confirmed attackers compromised its Commander platform, while operators reported thousands of miners redirected to an unfamiliar pool.

Bitcoin mining operators faced a suspected large-scale hijacking over the weekend after thousands of machines were allegedly redirected to the OCEAN mining pool without authorization.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 15, mining infrastructure provider CoreX Hosting raised the alarm that mining equipment was being redirected to OCEAN and that rewards were being assigned to a single Bitcoin address.

BTC enthusiast GalaxyMind estimated that the attack affected approximately 64,000 Bitcoin mining machines, redirecting 13 exahashes per second (EH/s) of computing power since around 8 p.m. Central Time on Nov. 14.

Blockchain security firm CoinSpect added that the redirected computing power represented approximately 1.5% of Bitcoin's global hashrate.

The incident threatened miners' earnings because the unauthorized changes directed rewards away from their intended recipients while their equipment continued consuming electricity and processing transactions.

CoreX subsequently reported that it was restoring affected miners to their original configurations and believed it had isolated the program responsible for the unauthorized changes.

The tech giant later declared the incident over after the computing power associated with the suspicious address reportedly fell to approximately 100 petahashes per second (PH/s), down from the previously reported 13 EH/s.

Still, blockchain records show that the Bitcoin address identified in CoreX's original warning had received mining rewards. Data from OCEAN shows three payments totaling 0.24308905 BTC between Nov. 15 and Nov. 16.

Sources indicate that dashed line: destination named by the host. Solid line: confirmed coinbase credit to that address.

The host's report and the block record establish different facts about the same address.

The transaction does not identify the controller or prove which incident shares generated the reward.

The transaction does not identify the controller or prove which incident shares generated the reward.

OCEAN's TIDES reward system allows previously submitted mining work to qualify for payments from later blocks. Consequently, rewards can keep arriving after mining activity stops.

While the central cause of the attack remains unknown, Bitcoin mining technology manufacturer Luxor confirmed that its Commander mining-management platform suffered a security breach that allowed unauthorized changes to customers' mining configurations.

“Last night our internal monitoring alerted us to an unauthorized redirect of hashrate through Commander…over a dozen client accounts. Affected machines were pointed to a different pool for a limited window. No data was leaked or exfiltrated from our systems.”.

The firm's engineering team patched Commander within two hours and began restoring affected machines to their original mining pools. It also promised full compensation for the redirected computing power.

Luxor CEO Nick Hansen attributed the compromise to a “sophisticated AI-enabled vector,” saying the attack began around 6 p.m. Pacific time on Nov. 14.

According to recent reports, hansen apologized to affected customers and warned that cryptocurrency companies were facing an increasingly aggressive wave of AI-powered attacks. He mentioned:.

“At this moment, anyone running any sort of substantial business, especially in crypto, is inundated with AI-enabled attacks. Abliterated models are running 24/7 against your entire surface, looking for a little crack, which they then use to (almost instantly) expand. This does not seem to be slowing down; rather, it's speeding up as models get better and more attackers enter the arena.”.

He revealed that Luxor had acquired dedicated GPUs to run its own modified AI models for defensive security testing and had suspended much of its fresh feature development to harden its infrastructure.

Luxor has not disclosed the precise method used to compromise Commander or confirmed GalaxyMind's estimates of 64,000 affected machines and 13 EH/s.

The tech giant has promised a full post-mortem, which could establish how the attackers gained access, the actual extent of the disruption, and whether the reported computing power was entirely linked to its compromised platform.

Hyperliquid's derivatives business has grown large enough to challenge some familiar centralised exchange names on a key measure: open interest. A third-quarter research report put positions open on the platform at approximately $16.8 billion at the end of September, a major increase over the previous quarter. For a decentralised trading venue, the scale is striking. But comparing it with conventional exchanges requires more than ranking a single number.

Open interest is the value of contracts that remain outstanding, not the amount of cash a venue has collected in fees or the value of trades settled that day. It reveals participation and leverage, while leaving vital questions about market depth and resilience unanswered.

Recent findings suggest that the Block's report on Hyperliquid's Q3 figures described open interest reaching roughly $16.8 billion, nearly 80% above the level recorded at the end of June. The report compared that snapshot with data for exchanges including Bybit, Kraken and OKX, though rankings depend on which products, venues and measurement conventions are included.

The headline number suggests that traders are comfortable maintaining substantial derivative exposure on Hyperliquid. It does not prove that all of that exposure is unhedged directional speculation. Some participants may be market makers or arbitrageurs carrying positions that offset risk elsewhere, while other traders could be using leverage to express very concentrated views.

In a recent development, the same Q3 analysis estimated approximately $191 million in protocol revenue, an increase of about 21.7% from the second quarter but a decrease of roughly 36.5% compared with the year-earlier period. That contrast is a useful warning against assuming that more open contracts automatically translate into stronger year-on-year economics. Revenue depends on trading activity, fees and the mix of products used.

Stock-linked perpetual products were another standout, with reported quarterly trading volume of about $153.8 billion, up approximately 161% sequentially. Yet volume can be affected by incentives, volatility and the churn of high-frequency participants. Healthy trading infrastructure also needs reliable pricing, liquid order books and a credible process for handling extreme market moves.

Industry observers note that perpetual futures let traders maintain leveraged exposure without a fixed expiry date. That flexibility comes with funding payments, margin requirements and liquidation risk. During a sharp market decline, forced closing of positions can magnify volatility. A platform's decentralised components do not eliminate the economic risk of carrying leverage or the operational need for robust safeguards.

It has been revealed that this is particularly relevant after the week's crypto sell-off. Market watchers should compare open interest with trading volume, funding costs and liquidation activity rather than treating rising positions as inherently bullish. A platform can be technologically impressive and still host dangerous levels of speculative risk.

In a recent development, the rise of on-chain perpetuals adds to the broader discussion about where exchange activity should take place. NewsBTC's coverage of institutional interest in DeFi through Aave highlights that traditional crypto firms are exploring decentralised infrastructure. Meanwhile, Aave's reserve-factor debate illustrates the governance decisions that shape the economics of on-chain services.

Recent findings suggest that hyperliquid's Q3 performance is evidence that decentralised derivatives can operate at considerable scale. The harder test comes during severe volatility, when users will judge it on execution quality, orderly liquidations and transparent risk management. Those outcomes will say more about the durability of its position than any single exchange league table.

  • Industry observers note that EP Wealth Advisors, a California-based investment advisory firm with about $24.4 billion in securities holdings, has revealed that it held 18,400 shares in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI) as of Sept.
  • This was disclosed in the official SEC filing that the tech giant submitted to the commission on Nov.

It has been revealed that major U.S. wealth management company EP Wealth Advisors has revealed that it holds an investment in an XRP exchange-traded fund (ETF). This was disclosed in the company's latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Industry observers note that EP Wealth Advisors, a California-based investment advisory firm with about $24.4 billion in securities holdings, has revealed that it held 18,400 shares in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This was disclosed in the official SEC filing that the tech giant submitted to the commission on Nov. 13. The filing indicated that the investment was valued at $147,936 at the end of the third quarter.

According to recent reports, furthermore, the filing indicated that the total portfolio value reported by EP Wealth Advisors stood at $24,380,879,896. This value comprises 1,603 items in the tech giant's 13F information table.

It's worth noting, however, that this isn't the manufacturer's total assets under management. It's the value of its reportable securities holdings. There are also assets that are not included in Form 13F.

It has been revealed that interestingly, this isn't the first time EP Wealth Advisors has held an investment in XRPI. Data from its historical 13F filings reveals that in the second quarter of 2026, the wealth management firm held 13,425 shares in XRPI.

It has been revealed that the recent filing indicates that the firm has now increased the number of shares it holds in the XRP ETF by 4,975 shares. This represents about a 37% increase in the company's XRPI holdings during the third quarter.

Nevertheless, this amount is very small relative to the company's multibillion-dollar securities portfolio. It represents less than 0.01% of the total value of its reported securities holdings.

It's also worth reiterating that Form 13F is simply a filing that shows institutional holdings at the end of a quarter. It doesn't necessarily represent the investment manager's current holdings.

Industry observers note that the Volatility Shares XRP ETF was rolled out in May 2025. Its ticker symbol is XRPI, and it is right now trading on Nasdaq.

According to recent reports, XRPI isn't a spot XRP ETF. This means it doesn't directly hold the cryptocurrency XRP. Rather, it primarily derives its exposure to XRP's price movements through XRP futures contracts.

This ETF essentially provides investors with a way to invest in XRP without actually having to hold or custody the cryptocurrency. The ETF aims to deliver investment returns that correlate with the performance of XRP.

As of Nov. 13, the most recent available data from the fund issuer reveals that XRPI's net assets stood at about $77.9 million.

#693. Bitcoin’s 1,000-Day Halving Pattern Returns

Bitcoin’s 1,000-Day Halving Pattern Returns

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/bitcoins-1000-day-halving-pattern-returns/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin may be approaching one of the most interesting technical windows of its current market cycle.
  • The analysis comes as Bitcoin trades near $64,282.54, according to the latest price provided at the time of writing, following a significant correction from its 2025 highs.
  • While traders continue debating whether the four-year cycle remains relevant, Bitcoinist recently examined how Bitcoin’s technical structure could avoid upcoming lows, highlighting the importance of reclaiming long-term moving averages.

Bitcoin may be approaching one of the most interesting technical windows of its current market cycle. A newly shared historical chart suggests that BTC has repeatedly broken major descending resistance lines around 1,000 days after a halving, raising questions about whether another recovery could be approaching.

The analysis comes as Bitcoin trades near $64,282.54, according to the latest price provided at the time of writing, following a significant correction from its 2025 highs.

While traders continue debating whether the four-year cycle remains relevant, Bitcoinist recently examined how Bitcoin’s technical structure could avoid upcoming lows, highlighting the importance of reclaiming long-term moving averages.

Now, another historical pattern is attracting attention.

On November 16, Rand Group shared a chart credited to analyst Jesse Olson, highlighting an unusual similarity between previous Bitcoin halving cycles.

The analysis suggests that Bitcoin’s 2016 and 2020 cycles broke their post-peak descending trendlines around day 1,000 after their respective halvings.

The chart overlays several cycles, using the number of days after each halving to compare their price structures.

According to Rand Group, the current cycle is approaching the same historical window.

Using the April 20, 2024 halving date, November 16, 2026 represents approximately day 940, leaving around 60 days before the 1,000-day milestone.

The historical comparison is particularly interesting because both previous breakouts occurred after extended periods of declining prices.

However, the pattern does not establish that Bitcoin must repeat its earlier performance.

The Bitcoin halving history confirms the dates used to compare the cycles, but the descending trendlines and their breakout timing remain the analyst’s interpretation.

The central question is whether Bitcoin’s current price structure supports the possibility of another trend reversal.

At approximately $64,282, Bitcoin remains below the immediate $65,000 resistance area.

A sustained recovery above that threshold could provide the first indication of improving short-term momentum.

However, stronger confirmation would require BTC to reclaim higher resistance around $68,000 and $70,000.

From a technical perspective, a descending trendline connects a series of lower highs.

Breaking above that line suggests selling pressure may be weakening, but traders generally look for additional confirmation through stronger volume and successful retests.

The Relative Strength Index is another key indicator.

A sustained move above 50 could suggest improving bullish momentum, particularly if Bitcoin simultaneously establishes higher lows.

Conversely, continued rejection below resistance would indicate that the broader downtrend remains intact.

The $62,000 region represents an notable downside reference, followed by the psychological $60,000 level.

Historical cycle analysis has become increasingly popular as investors search for signs of a market bottom.

Bitcoinist previously covered an analyst’s Bitcoin cycle timing model, which similarly examined recurring intervals between major market turning points.

Nevertheless, exact timing models can be misleading when they rely on a small number of historical observations.

Bitcoin’s current market structure is also different from earlier cycles.

Institutional participation, exchange-traded funds, and changing global liquidity conditions could influence how future recoveries develop.

Another Bitcoinist analysis explored the possibility of a historical Bitcoin fakeout, demonstrating why investors should consider alternative scenarios before treating recurring chart formations as guaranteed outcomes.

The strongest bullish signal would not simply be reaching day 1,000.

Instead, it would be a confirmed breakout above descending resistance, supported by improving volume, momentum, and market structure.

Bitcoin’s approaching 1,000-day milestone offers an intriguing historical comparison.

If the pattern highlighted by Rand Group repeats, the coming weeks could become an vital period for traders watching the end of the current downtrend.

We believe the technical evidence deserves attention, particularly if Bitcoin begins reclaiming resistance levels and establishing a sequence of higher lows.

However, historical similarities alone cannot confirm a market bottom.

For now, $65,000 remains the first resistance area to monitor, followed by $68,000 and $70,000.

A convincing breakout through these levels could strengthen the case for a broader recovery.

Until then, the 1,000-day halving pattern remains a potentially bullish setup awaiting confirmation.

Aster’s CEO attributed the extreme volatility to highly leveraged liquidations but remarked the exchange remained operational.

Aster CEO Leonard Leung says the team is investigating a sharp swing in its ASTER token after a volatile trading session that sent the price above $0.71 before crashing back to $0.48 in just over 15 minutes.

Leung attributed the volatility to liquidations of highly leveraged positions, which he said were “likely malicious,” although the team was still investigating the incident.

Leung also said Aster’s operations were functioning normally and that the episode was unrelated to ASTER market-making arrangements.

The token later recovered to around $0.55, up 4.5% over the previous 24 hours but still roughly 22.5% below its intraday peak.

The swings came alongside heavy derivatives trading. CoinGlass recorded about $1.29 billion in ASTER futures volume over 24 hours, up 121% from the day before, while 24-hour spot volume was $118.3 million, up 67% from the day before.

Meanwhile, tracked liquidations totaled approximately $9.1 million, including $5.97 million in long positions and $3.14 million in shorts.

ASTER is the native token of Aster, a decentralized exchange offering leveraged perpetual futures trading. The token supports governance and community rewards, while the protocol uses a portion of its revenue to buy back ASTER.

Sources indicate that A confrontation between Louisiana officials and the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission is sharpening the dispute over who gets to regulate prediction markets. The state has pursued restrictions on certain event-contract offerings, while the federal agency has gone to court asserting its authority. The dispute could affect platforms offering sports and other outcome-based contracts, but the legal arguments have not yet produced a final nationwide answer.

Sources indicate that it is a case where the exact stage of litigation matters. Temporary orders, complaints and jurisdictional claims are not final findings about which side is right.

Industry observers note that the Block reported that a Louisiana state court issued a temporary restraining order on November 12 involving a group of prediction-market and related businesses. The state's approach seeks to require geographic restrictions for certain offerings that it indicates should not be available without appropriate state authorisation. Firms named in the proceedings reportedly include Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase and Robinhood among a wider set.

An order of this kind is designed to address immediate concerns while further litigation continues. Its existence does not establish that every product mentioned is unlawful under all circumstances. Different platforms may offer different types of contracts, and the precise language of the order and subsequent court rulings determines what each respondent must do.

The CFTC filed a federal complaint on November 13 as the dispute escalated. Federal commodities law gives the agency crucial powers over derivatives markets, but state authorities have their own responsibilities for gambling and consumer protection. The central legal question is where one set of powers ends and the other begins when an event contract resembles both a derivative and a bet on an outcome.

In a recent development, the disagreement is not merely political theatre. Companies need clear boundaries to decide which products may be offered, how customers must be screened and what licences or approvals are necessary. Conflicting instructions from different levels of government can be expensive to implement and difficult for customers to understand.

For an operator, an adverse ruling might mean geofencing customers, suspending products or changing contract design. For people, it might affect whether an existing market remains accessible in their location and what protections apply if a dispute arises. These potential consequences make the litigation commercially significant even before the courts resolve the larger federalism question.

NewsBTC's earlier account of CFTC-related litigation involving Coinbase and Kalshi offers useful background on the expanding legal debate around event and derivative markets. A single case, however, should not be treated as decisive precedent for every possible contract category.

Reporting identifies November 30 as a date to watch in the Louisiana proceedings. Whether temporary restrictions remain in force, are modified or expire can depend on procedural developments before then. Readers should also monitor the federal case independently, as it may follow a different timetable and raise distinct legal questions.

In a recent development, other jurisdictions are wrestling with how to supervise fresh financial infrastructure, including tokenisation standards in Europe. Louisiana's dispute is a particularly sharp example of the same underlying problem: innovation does not arrive organised according to existing regulator boundaries. Until courts and lawmakers clarify those boundaries, platforms will continue to operate amid uncertainty rather than a settled national rulebook.

Industry News: Vitalik Buterin Breaks Silence on Upcoming Ethereum (ETH) Update

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has published a lengthy post on EIP-8037, a change planned for the Glamsterdam upgrade. In his latest post, Buterin wrote that something like EIP-8037 is, unfortunately, the only way for Ethereum to scale safely.

With the upgrade, Ethereum will collect an additional gas fee for the creation of newly introduced accounts. Creating a new account would cost more than five times as much gas as it does now, with new storage slots and contracts getting more expensive too.

According to Buterin, execution is easy to scale, but Ethereum's state already grows by around 110 GiB per year, and every node has to keep it.

In a recent development, unfortunately, it will bring more pressure on existing contracts, for example, the OP Stack bridge. The bridge has a hardcoded gas limit of 40,000, and even a small increase in state gas costs would push its operation above it. Mainnet has at least 13 contracts like that, according to the security firm ChainSecurity.

It's a double-edged sword: from one standpoint, it limits the ability of spammers and scammers to fill the network with junk accounts used by illicit actors; from the other, it creates additional financial pressure.

Glamsterdam being postponed is another pain factor here: considering the poor state of the market and Ethereum's struggle, it's clear that any delays in major updates negatively affect the network outlook. The new date is yet to be confirmed.

Vitalik Buterin has been hinting at the change in gas consumption for ages now. Back in 2024, he called multidimensional gas the hardest problem in his own post on the topic.

In a recent development, setting strict limits was never a farsighted option, and developers have been told that for years. However, it's yet another question: who's actually to blame? Buterin himself admitted that this rule hasn't been written down or repeated since 2021, so newer developers simply didn't know about it.

He now suggests writing down a list of features that are likely to change, from gas mechanics to slot time.

Meta is reportedly experimenting with a prediction game for employees in which participants forecast outcomes using points rather than real money. That may sound like a small internal product test, but it offers an interesting window into how large technology companies are thinking about forecasting, social engagement and the mechanics behind prediction markets.

The essential distinction is that a points-based game is not automatically a cash-settled financial market. No public launch or real-money service has been confirmed in the reporting on the experiment, so it would be misleading to describe Meta as having entered the regulated betting or event-contract business.

Sources indicate that the Block, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported that Meta was testing an employee application known as Takes, previously called Arena. Participants can make forecasts and earn or lose an internal points balance referred to as cred. The structure resembles a prediction market in some respects, but without the same money flows or legal arrangements as a traded contract.

It has been revealed that an internal trial can help answer useful product questions. Do people enjoy making forecasts? How should results be scored? Does a ranking system reward genuine insight or simply encourage attention-grabbing guesses? Those questions matter whether the eventual outcome is a staff game, a public social feature or nothing at all. The existence of a test does not establish which direction Meta will choose.

It has been revealed that real-money prediction markets can involve financial risk, market manipulation concerns, customer eligibility, settlement disputes and questions about gambling or derivatives law. A points-based contest may avoid some of those features, depending on its design. But a game can still have integrity problems if employees feel encouraged to trade on private information or if forecasts become workplace performance signals.

There is also a difference between a prediction with a numerical score and a security or derivative. Those categories are shaped by contract terms and applicable law, not simply by whether the interface looks like a market. Readers should be cautious when comparing an internal staff experiment directly with companies offering event contracts to paying customers.

Recent findings suggest that regulated prediction markets are attracting scrutiny from federal and state authorities, particularly around sports-related contracts. NewsBTC previously examined a CFTC-related lawsuit involving Coinbase and Kalshi, an example of how disputes over jurisdiction can arise as firms offer products that do not fit neatly into traditional categories.

It has been revealed that that uncertainty makes Meta's use of non-cash points noteworthy. A platform can learn about user participation and forecasting behaviour without immediately building the custody, settlement and compliance systems required for real-money products. Whether that is the strategic reason for the design has not been established; it is simply a material distinction between the two models.

Massive companies routinely trial features that never reach the public. Employee feedback can reveal problems early, and an internal rename does not by itself mean a product is ready for commercial deployment. Similarly, parallels with AI-agent payment experiments covered by NewsBTC show how companies use small tests to explore unfamiliar transaction designs before the market is settled.

Industry observers note that the next meaningful development would be an official description of the experiment's objectives, product scope or possible external release. Until then, Takes is best understood as a reported internal forecasting test — an interesting sign of curiosity, but not evidence that Meta has introduced a new exchange.

  • Recent findings suggest that bitcoin traders are facing an unusual situation.
  • In a recent development, the development comes after Bitcoin’s latest correction pushed the cryptocurrency toward its lowest levels in months.
  • Now, with traders increasingly focused on downside protection, an vital question is emerging: Could the market’s defensive positioning eventually create the conditions for an unexpected Bitcoin recovery?

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin traders are facing an unusual situation. A massive $900 million options position has emerged as the largest on Deribit, but the real surprise is where that position sits: $60,000.

In a recent development, the development comes after Bitcoin’s latest correction pushed the cryptocurrency toward its lowest levels in months. As we recently reported, Bitcoin briefly fell below $63,000, before recovering above $64,000.

Now, with traders increasingly focused on downside protection, an vital question is emerging: Could the market’s defensive positioning eventually create the conditions for an unexpected Bitcoin recovery?

Bitcoin’s $60,000 put options have overtaken the previously dominant $100,000 calls on Deribit, reaching approximately $900 million in notional open interest.

The $100,000 calls, meanwhile, have fallen to roughly $867 million.

This reversal is particularly interesting because the two contracts represent very different market expectations.

Call options provide exposure to potential price increases, while put options can be used to profit from declines or protect existing Bitcoin holdings.

However, the change does not necessarily mean investors suddenly placed $900 million in fresh bearish bets.

Open interest measures outstanding contracts accumulated over time. The decline in $100,000 call positions also reflects traders reducing earlier bullish exposure.

Investors can monitor the latest positioning through Deribit’s official options statistics.

The shift highlights how the options market has become increasingly defensive, even as Bitcoin continues attracting long-term institutional interest.

From a technical perspective, the $60,000 region deserves close attention.

Bitcoin recently declined toward $62,000 before staging a partial recovery, suggesting buyers remain active around the lower end of the current trading range.

However, a temporary bounce is not the same as a confirmed bullish reversal.

The first important area to monitor is the recent $62,000 low. Holding above this region would suggest that buyers are attempting to establish a short-term base.

A move above $65,000 could provide an initial sign of improving momentum, while a sustained recovery toward $68,000–$70,000 would offer a more meaningful test of overhead resistance.

The 50-period and 200-period exponential moving averages are also important.

If Bitcoin reclaims both indicators while the RSI moves above 50, the technical outlook could begin improving.

Conversely, a sustained breakdown below $62,000 would increase the risk of another test of the psychologically important $60,000 level.

These are potential scenarios, not confirmed breakout signals.

The most interesting possibility is that defensive market positioning could eventually help amplify a recovery.

When sentiment becomes heavily bearish, an unexpected rise in Bitcoin’s price can force leveraged short sellers to close their positions.

This process, known as a short squeeze, can accelerate upward momentum.

Bitcoinist recently examined how an analyst is buying Bitcoin during the correction, highlighting the possibility that improving liquidity and market structure could support a recovery.

However, put-option open interest should not be confused with short futures positions. Large put holdings alone do not demonstrate that a short squeeze is imminent.

Another notable factor is the recent wave of liquidations.

As previously covered, Bitcoin’s market sell-off triggered over $1.6 billion in liquidations, removing substantial leveraged exposure from the cryptocurrency market.

Such events can intensify short-term volatility, but they can also reduce excessive leverage.

The options market is sending an important signal: traders are increasingly concerned about protecting their positions.

Nevertheless, the $900 million concentration around $60,000 does not guarantee another major decline.

For now, we believe Bitcoin’s ability to hold above its recent lows will be critical.

A recovery through $65,000, followed by stronger volume and improving momentum indicators, could begin challenging the current bearish narrative.

If buyers eventually reclaim $68,000–$70,000, attention could shift toward whether the latest correction has established a sustainable bottom.

The $60,000 options position may be dominating headlines, but Bitcoin’s next decisive move will ultimately depend on spot demand, liquidity, and whether buyers can regain control of the trend.

Tech Report: Brazil Takes Aim at Stablecoins With Shocking Money Laundering Claim

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read | Sumber: https://u.today/brazil-takes-aim-at-stablecoins-with-shocking-money-laundering-claim

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.
  • The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.
  • According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.

The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.

According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

Romantini claimed that funds acquired legally could be transformed once they enter the stablecoin ecosystem.

In his view, even legally obtained money could effectively be "dirtied" if used in certain stablecoin schemes, and thus be considered part of a money laundering operation.

It’s crucial to note that the comments attributed to Romantini do not represent an official statement that all conversions into stablecoins could be considered money laundering.

This statement comes as Brazil has already moved to tighten restrictions on how cryptocurrencies are used for international payments.

Industry observers note that on April 30, the Central Bank of Brazil published Resolution No. 561, which took effect on Oct. 1.

The resolution limits the use of virtual assets for the settlement of international payment and transfer services, also known as eFX.

In practice, this means that payments between an eFX provider and its foreign partner must be settled through traditional foreign exchange operations or a Brazilian real account opened by nonresidents.

Crypto payments for these particular settlements are off-limits.

A practice called the "stablecoin sandwich" is particularly concerning.

The way it works is that a Brazilian fintech accepts a certain amount of reais from a customer, then uses this money to purchase stablecoins like USDT or USDC and sends the funds in crypto to an offshore tech giant.

This firm, in turn, can convert these stablecoins into fiat currency to make payments or send money to families.

This allows people to make international money transfers for a lower fee and circumvent some of the infrastructure banks use.

The controversial statements have already received a response from Brazil’s crypto industry.

In a statement on Nov. 14, the Brazilian Association of Tokenization and Digital Assets (ABToken) questioned the alleged classification of stablecoin transactions as money laundering.

ABToken maintains that the use of stablecoins is not necessarily illegal.

Furthermore, the association also cautioned that sweeping bans may create legal confusion and hinder legitimate business activities that use stablecoins for international payments.

The discussions reportedly follow efforts by supporters in Silicon Valley to persuade the manufacturer’s board to reconsider his departure.

One supporter reportedly described plans to assemble a group of technology executives to advocate for Huang’s reinstatement and seek support from the White House.

The developments represent an unexpected turn for Nvidia, which announced Huang’s resignation on November 12 and appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

Huang’s departure followed reports concerning his personal relationships and questions about the tech giant’s China-related business dealings. Nvidia’s board had previously unveiled an independent investigation into concerns involving a possible foreign intelligence effort.

Despite the controversy, Huang remains closely associated with Nvidia’s transformation into one of the most influential companies in artificial intelligence.

His possible return could therefore have significant implications for investor confidence, although the board has not announced any decision to reinstate him.

When uncertainty spreads across major technology companies, investors sometimes reduce exposure to risk-sensitive assets.

Ethereum price is approaching another notable technical turning point as co-founder Vitalik Buterin expresses renewed optimism about a proposal that could accelerate the network’s transition toward quantum-resistant cryptography.

The development has attracted attention across the cryptocurrency community, raising questions about whether Ethereum’s improving long-term technological outlook could eventually support stronger demand for ETH.

The announcement comes as Ethereum continues navigating a challenging market environment. As we recently reported, Ethereum whales are buying the dip, with large holders accumulating ETH around important support levels. This activity could become particularly significant if buyers regain control of short-term momentum.

On November 16, Buterin shared a detailed explanation of leanPCS, a cryptographic approach associated with Ethereum Improvement Proposal 8288.

His comments marked a significant change in his assessment of the technology.

Over the past few weeks I’ve gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull.

Buterin explained that Ethereum faces an important technical challenge as it prepares to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography.

Industry observers note that traditional Ethereum transaction signatures are relatively small. However, quantum-resistant signatures and advanced cryptographic proofs can require significantly more data, potentially increasing network costs.

According to the official Ethereum EIP-8288 proposal, the proposed architecture would aggregate cryptographic signatures and proofs into a single recursive STARK, potentially reducing the data requirements associated with quantum-resistant transactions.

The approach could eventually support more efficient transactions, stronger cryptographic security, and greater flexibility for developers.

However, EIP-8288 remains a draft proposal. Its potential benefits have not yet been deployed across Ethereum’s mainnet.

While Buterin’s comments provide a potentially encouraging long-term development, Ethereum’s immediate price outlook depends on whether buyers can regain control of the market.

The $2,000 region represents an notable psychological threshold, particularly after the cryptocurrency’s recent weakness.

Recent analysis of Ethereum’s accumulation trend highlights another crucial development: the share of ETH held in staking has reached record levels, suggesting continued commitment among long-term holders.

A sustained recovery above $2,000 would be an encouraging initial signal, but traders should also examine the four-hour chart for confirmation.

The 50-period exponential moving average can help identify changes in short-term momentum, while the 200-period EMA provides a broader view of the prevailing trend.

If ETH moves above both indicators and successfully retests them as support, the recovery scenario would become more convincing.

However, if the price remains below these moving averages, upward movements could represent temporary relief rallies rather than a confirmed trend reversal.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) provides another notable signal.

A sustained move above 50 would suggest improving momentum, particularly if accompanied by stronger trading volume. Conversely, an RSI reading below 50 would indicate that sellers still retain an advantage.

For now, traders should prioritize confirmation rather than assuming that positive technological developments will immediately translate into higher prices.

Ethereum’s long-term investment narrative increasingly depends on its ability to remain secure, scalable, and useful as blockchain technology evolves.

Quantum computing presents a potential future challenge to existing cryptographic systems, making Ethereum’s preparation an notable part of its development roadmap.

Bitcoinist previously reported that Ethereum researchers prioritized quantum security, demonstrating how post-quantum protection has become an increasingly key part of the network’s development roadmap.

The proposed EIP-8288 architecture could help reduce the costs associated with verifying larger signatures and advanced cryptographic proofs.

For institutional customers and developers, greater efficiency and security could strengthen Ethereum’s attractiveness as a platform for financial applications.

However, the relationship between technological improvements and ETH’s market value is not automatic.

The daily chart will be particularly important for determining whether Ethereum is building a longer-term recovery structure.

A sequence of higher lows, improving trading volume, and a sustained move above the 200-day moving average would provide stronger evidence of a trend reversal.

Until those conditions emerge, investors should distinguish between Ethereum’s long-term technological potential and its shorter-term market performance.

Buterin’s growing confidence in leanPCS represents an encouraging development for Ethereum’s future security and scalability.

Nevertheless, the cryptocurrency’s next major move will depend on whether buyers can establish stronger technical momentum.

We believe the combination of Ethereum’s continuing development and improving price structure could create a more favorable environment for ETH over time.

The immediate challenge remains reclaiming $2,000 and establishing a sustainable pattern of higher lows.

If buyers achieve that, attention could shift toward the next resistance zones identified on the daily chart.

For now, Ethereum’s quantum-resistant roadmap provides an important long-term narrative, while technical indicators will determine whether the current market recovery has enough strength to continue.

Neither firm is backing away. In fact, both are positioning themselves for a recovery that could dramatically revalue their massive crypto treasuries. The question is which strategy has the better chance of delivering the biggest payoff.

That is a substantial paper loss, but Saylor’s accumulation strategy has never depended on buying every Bitcoin at the bottom. Strategy continues using capital markets to expand its position, betting that Bitcoin’s long-term appreciation will eventually overwhelm short-term volatility.

Its latest filing also revealed $244.7 million in proceeds from common stock sales. Strategy allocated $33.4 million toward Bitcoin purchases, while spending $228.1 million repurchasing its STRC preferred shares.

🧵1/BitMine provided its latest holdings update for November 16, 2026$11.8 billion in total crypto + "moonshots":– 6,077,745 ETH at $1,823 per ETH (per @coinbase)– 216 Bitcoin (BTC)– $180 million stake in Beast Industries @MrBeast– $67 million stake in Eightco Holdings….

At recent prices around $1,820, those holdings are worth $11 billion. But BitMine has another advantage that Strategy cannot replicate with its Bitcoin treasury: staking income.

Sources indicate that that creates a potentially powerful combination. BitMine is accumulating a substantial share of Ethereum’s supply while putting most of its holdings to work.

Lee’s thesis extends beyond ETH price appreciation. He sees Ethereum benefiting from institutional tokenization, financial infrastructure moving onchain, and growing demand for blockchain-based settlement.

If those trends accelerate, BitMine could benefit from both Ethereum appreciation and recurring staking rewards.

Industry observers note that this is where the competition gets interesting. Strategy has the larger dollar-denominated crypto treasury, but BitMine has a compelling argument for capital efficiency. Bitcoin offers a straightforward scarcity thesis, while Ethereum adds staking and exposure to expanding blockchain activity.

Sources indicate that strategy’s biggest advantage is its enormous Bitcoin position. With 850,849 BTC, even a substantial recovery in Bitcoin could translate into billions of dollars in additional treasury value.

In a recent development, bitMine, however, has built an Ethereum position approaching 5% of circulating supply. Its staking operation gives the company another potential source of returns while waiting for the next market expansion.

According to recent reports, there is also a difference in what investors are buying. Strategy offers a concentrated Bitcoin treasury vehicle, while BitMine offers a leveraged corporate bet on Ethereum’s future financial infrastructure.

Our verdict? BitMine has the more productive treasury model, but Strategy remains the heavyweight in corporate crypto accumulation.

If Bitcoin leads the next recovery, Saylor could swiftly reclaim the spotlight. If Ethereum outperforms and institutional adoption accelerates, Lee’s strategy could look considerably smarter.

Both companies are effectively making the same bet: today’s market weakness will look insignificant when the next major crypto cycle arrives.

Sources indicate that the winner may ultimately depend on which asset leads that recovery. But neither Saylor nor Lee appears interested in waiting for confirmation before accumulating.
